description:
n + 1 with both operands known integers lowers to a direct call of Kernel.+ whose result is delivered to a resume entry: the caller is split in two, the rest of the body's live values are captured in a closure, and fz_op_add_ii runs behind deliver_lanes. Seen in the backend dump of walk(<<c, r :: binary>>, n) -> walk(r, n + 1): 'tail direct_call +(v1, 1) -> deliver e1', e1 captures r. About 26% of the plain walk after inline reads.

Investigated (read-only, develop at 76cf77155):
- First departure from 'one add': the front end. A binary operator in a body is a call to a Kernel function (src/compiler2/jobs/body.rs, Expr::BinOp via direct_operator_name: + - * / % == != < <= > >=), before any type is known. fz_ir has no add/sub/mul primitive.
- Every non-tail call splits. plan_steps/plan_continuation (jobs/body.rs) make a DeliveredResume entry unless the call is the last thing in its block. There is no leaf or plain-return call form; no property of the callee is consulted. EffectSummary has no consumer but the dump.
- After planning, Kernel.+[int,int] is one tail call to the extern wrapper of fz_op_add_ii (checked return: i64 overflow raises ArithmeticError; there are no bignums). So the chain is caller -> +[int,int] -> wrapper -> runtime fn -> return_call_indirect into the continuation closure.
- Same position: - * / % div rem, < <= > >= ==, byte_size, length, elem, hd, tl, tuple_size, abs, <> (guarded Kernel functions over an extern). and/or/not are inlined as case. The same operators in a guard are inline PatternGuardExpr nodes with no call.
- In four backend dumps, about 100 of 213 delivered call sites are Kernel operators and scalar wrappers.
- Existing parts that could serve: native lowering already turns an entry with a single direct transfer into a block of the transferring function (EntryFns::for_entries); guards already emit an extern inline (lower_guard_extern); the checked-extern wrapper is already 'one primitive, raise on failure'. Candidate rule: in native lowering, a delivered call whose target resolves to an extern wrapper is the extern call, its failure check, and a direct transfer to the resume entry, which then becomes a block. The interpreter is unchanged.
- A test can pin a call site's return flow through BackendProgramCapture (src/compiler2/drive_test.rs).

Size in the distiller (profile, 16,000 lines): closure capture and code reads are about 3.5% of samples in runtime calls; the share inside compiled code is not measured. Map puts (23%) and field reads (10%) come first. Next step: a spike of the candidate rule on the walk and the distiller with a prediction, then a proposal page. Evidence: scratchpad b183-5/walkd.backend, walkd.clif; arith/tally.py.

comments.text:
Spike result (throwaway worktree ../fz-sc8-197 on #585 + uniq + names, build path, switch FZ_SPIKE_ARITH; patch in session scratch arith197/spike-arith.patch, 1 file, jobs/native.rs). I re-ran the binaries.
Rule: a delivered direct call whose callee is an extern, or a one-clause forwarder with no dispatch and no steps that tail-calls an extern with the same parameters, is emitted as the extern call inline (Prim::Extern), its checked-failure branch into emit_raise, and a transfer to the resume entry, which EntryFns::for_entries then makes a block of the caller. No continuation is built.
Instructions retired, off -> on: byte walk 129.7G -> 72.7G (27.8 -> 15.7 ns/byte); index walk 192.4G -> 72.4G (37.5 -> 12.9 ns/byte); distiller 32,000 lines 28.80G -> 24.95G (-13.4%), stdout identical, user time 1.39 -> 1.06 s in one back-to-back pair. Predictions (19 ns, 15 ns, <=27G) all held or were beaten.
Reduction yields on the byte walk fell 125,829 -> 83,886: the removed call was a reduction.
Not done in the spike: machine add/sub/compare inline (still calls fz_op_add_ii, 2% of samples); interp; the rule is derived twice (at for_entries and at emission); stack trace no longer has the Kernel.+ frame (message unchanged).

Generalisation (page version 2): the rule is 'a call splits its caller only when the callee can suspend'. Prompt = extern, or a function all of whose calls are direct calls to prompt callees (least fixpoint from externs, so recursion never concludes prompt; closure calls are not prompt).
Counted on the distiller's backend dump (#585 base; scratch arith197/dist.backend.txt + prompt.py): 1,375 executables, 115 externs, 495 prompt; 1,073 delivered direct call sites, 552 with a prompt callee (51%); 314 closure-call tails. Static count, not executed share.
Safety facts read in code: a process is collected only at CollectionBoundary::Yield | Park (runtime/src/process.rs; one call in sched_core), so prompt code never meets a collection. Guards already evaluate inline: PatternGuardExpr::{Binary, Extern, Dispatch}; comparisons map to IrBinOp inline (jobs/native.rs ~5696), also implemented in native_codegen/receive.rs and ir_interp/dispatch_exec.rs.
Second general rule: a clause that only tail-calls with its own parameters is its target (call-edge resolution).
EffectSummary (allocates, observable, halts, calls_opaque) has no reader but the dump: proposed for deletion.

Experiments (predictions written before the data).
E-trace (done): uncaught integer overflow with the narrow spike off and on prints the same text ('** (ArithmeticError) bad argument in arithmetic expression', exit 1); no stack trace is printed either way. A bad-typed operand is a compile error (spec/violation), so it never reaches run time. Hypothesis 'the raise site changes observable output' is refuted for uncaught errors.
E-count (running): per-site execution counters in the built distiller (32,000 lines), joined to the prompt classification of the same build's backend dump.
 P1: of executed delivered direct calls, 55-75% have a prompt callee (program text says 51%).
 P2: the narrow spike's shape (extern or forwarder) accounts for at least 60% of those executed prompt calls; the wide rule adds at least 25% more executed calls on top of the narrow one. If the wide rule adds under 10%, it buys the fold but little speed.
 P3: the top 15 call sites by count are dominated by Kernel operators on known types and by the JSON decoder's helpers.
E-wide (after E-count): spike of prompt functions returning in registers; only worth running if P2 holds.

E-count result (distiller, 32,000 lines, 20.66 MB; counters in scratch sitecount/, analysis cls.py). Executed delivered direct calls: 21,868,584 (683 per line).
 P1 held: callee prompt 12,921,685 = 59.1% (predicted 55-75%).
 P2 held: the narrow spike's shape is 9,592,631 = 43.9% of all (74% of the prompt ones); prompt-but-not-narrow is 3,329,054 = 15.2% of all, i.e. the wide rule removes 35% more executed calls than the narrow one. Largest: JSON.string -> run_join 1,476,698; JSON.object_value -> Map.put 1,085,030; then Kernel.negate, Map.entry, Map.has_key?, Kernel.compare, Map.fetch.
 P3 held: top sites are run_join's two byte_size and its '-', digits' * - +, and the decoder's helpers.
 New: 40.9% (8,946,899) have a callee that is not prompt, and nearly all of it is tail-recursive leaf loops in the decoder: skip_ws alone is 5,903,582 calls (27% of all executed delivered calls), then string 1,085,030, value 1,314,816, digits 515,774. skip_ws makes no calls but its own tail call. Under the bounded definition a recursive function is never prompt. Hypothesis to test: a function whose only non-prompt call is a tail call to itself can be called as a step too (its stack is bounded; what it loses is the yield inside the loop).
 Cost per removed call in the narrow spike: (28.80G - 24.95G) / 9,592,631 = about 400 instructions.
E-wide predictions (before the run): bounded prompt rule: 24.95G -> 23.9G or fewer; adding self-tail-recursive leaf loops: 21.8G or fewer.

E-wide result (throwaway; patch in scratch wide/spike-wide.patch; I re-ran the four distiller binaries, stdout identical in all).
Distiller 32,000 lines, instructions retired / binary size / executed continuation-building calls:
 off      28.81G  4,996,760 B  21.87M
 narrow   24.94G  4,444,072 B  12.28M   (-13.4%)
 prompt A 24.13G  4,274,120 B   9.41M   (-16.3%; predicted <=23.9G, missed by 0.8%)
 loops B  22.24G  4,154,296 B   3.63M   (-22.8%; predicted <=21.8G, missed by 1.9%)
Byte walk: 129.6G / 72.65G / 72.65G / 66.2G. Index walk: 192.4G / 72.3G / 72.3G / 66.5G.
Per call removed: narrow about 400 instructions; rule A adds 0.81G for 2.87M calls (about 285 each); rule B adds 1.89G for 5.78M calls (about 325 each).
Why A reached 402 prompt executables, not the 495 my script counted: the spike refuses callees with a dispatch-edge call (62), a NoReturn call to a raiser (49), or a zero-lane return (6 sites), and its extern test excludes unit/never/opaque returns. Those are spike limits, not limits of the rule.
The binary gets smaller at every step although prompt functions are compiled in two forms: the resume functions and delivery bodies removed outweigh the second forms.
Spike mechanics worth keeping in mind: a prompt form returns its lanes with a machine return (NativeEntryAbi::Prompt, Tail convention); a raise inside prompt code sets the process flags and returns placeholder lanes, and each prompt call site checks the flags (two loads and an or) and unwinds; 21 behaviour fixtures and two purpose-built programs print the same off and on. Rule B loops do not yield.
What remains (3.63M calls): the recursive parser itself (object_entry -> string, object_colon -> value, about 1.1M each).

Predictions for X1-X3, written before the data.

X1 extern heads, compile side. Throwaway: a one-clause forwarder (no dispatch, no steps, tail call to an extern with the same parameters) is resolved to its extern, so the forwarder executable is not in the backend program. Predictions: (1) the distiller backend program loses 35-45 of its 1,375 executables; (2) run-time instructions on 32,000 lines are within 1% of the narrow spike (24.94G); (3) compile jobs attributable to the forwarders are 2-4% of all jobs; (4) stdout identical. Falsifier: forwarders stay referenced (first-class use, dispatch edges) so fewer than 20 disappear.

X2 leaf loops. Known before the run: under rule B the byte walk p1b peaks at 5,858 MB against 674 MB, because a loop called promptly cannot yield and collections happen only at yields. (a) Measure the longest run of iterations of any leaf loop without a yield, on 32,000 lines and on the full log. Prediction: the maximum is no more than the longest line in bytes; the median run is under 20. (b) Bail variant: the loop counts reductions on its back edge; when the budget runs out it saves its arguments and returns a flag; the caller then builds the continuation it would have built today and enters the loop's ordinary entry. Loops are not prompt for the fixpoint; only calls from non-prompt callers take the fast path. Predictions: distiller instructions within 1.5% of rule B (at most 22.6G); p1b peak back to 674 MB +-5%; distiller peak at most 260 MB; reduction yields on the distiller within 5% of the unchanged compiler. Falsifier: the back-edge check costs more than 3% or the peak does not come back.

X3 guard fold (reading question). Prediction: the eight guard operators in PatternGuardBinOp, implemented three times (native, receive, interpreter), can be removed in favour of the route guards already use for byte_size, map_size and tuple_size (guard_dispatch into guard_extern), once comparison and arithmetic are extern heads. Falsifier: an operator whose meaning inside a guard differs from the Kernel function in a way the existing raise-means-guard-fails mapping does not cover.

X3 becomes a run. Reading found: arithmetic in a guard is already a call to the Kernel function (guard_expr_from_ast sends + - * / % and unary minus through guard_call_expr, which reifies the Kernel clauses as a helper plan ending in guard_extern). The six comparisons and and/or/not are separate operators with their own lowering in three places (jobs/native.rs, native_codegen/receive.rs, ir_interp/dispatch_exec.rs). Also found: fz_op_add_ii and friends are ordinary runtime functions reached by a C call, not inline instructions.
Experiment: behind a switch, send the six comparisons in guards through guard_call_expr like arithmetic. Predictions written before the run: (1) the build is refused or does not settle, because the last clause of Kernel.</2 is 'compare(left, right) < 0', so the helper for < refers to itself; == may have the same shape. (2) If it does build, distiller stdout is identical and run-time instructions rise by under 1% (an untyped guard comparison becomes a helper dispatch plus a C call where today it is an inline compare).

X3 result (develop c7edccd4a, release, switch FZ_SPIKE_GUARDCMP in a throwaway worktree; two edits: guard_expr_from_ast and walk_guard_calls).
- == and != in guards routed to Kernel.==/!=: builds; small probe output identical; distiller stdout identical; run 27.75G vs 27.76G instructions (no change); compile 16.17G -> 16.30G (+0.8%); binary +16,560 bytes. Prediction 2 held (under 1%).
- < <= > >= routed to Kernel: refused, 'compiler2 guard helper cycle detected: </2 -> </2' at Kernel.fz:1168. Prediction 1 held for the ordering family, not for equality (its last clause calls the extern fz_op_eq, no self reference).
- Cause of the cycle: the last clause is 'compare(left, right) < 0'; a guard helper is reified untyped, so the inner < (integer < integer) names the whole function again. A body does not have this problem because it selects the clause by type. Typed extern heads give the guard the same selection.
- Also read: a body already sends all eleven operators to Kernel (direct_operator_name in jobs/body.rs); a guard sends five (arithmetic_function). The two tables are one question asked twice.

X4 typed heads (the first half of an extern head). Typed clause heads already exist ('def is_integer(_ :: integer), do: true'). Experiment: rewrite the 48 Kernel clauses of the form 'def left OP right when is_T(left) and is_U(right), do: fz_op_*(...)' as 'def (left :: T) OP (right :: U), do: fz_op_*(...)'. Predictions before the run: (1) it builds and distiller stdout is identical; (2) compile instructions fall by 0.5% or more (no is_integer/is_float guard helpers to plan); (3) run instructions within 0.3%; (4) with FZ_SPIKE_GUARDCMP=all the cycle on </2 remains, because the helper is still reified without argument types.

X4 result (develop c7edccd4a, release). 48 Kernel clauses rewritten from 'when is_T(left) and is_U(right)' to typed heads. Builds; distiller stdout identical. The backend program dump is identical to the guarded form once source offsets are removed (0 differing lines of 96,764); telemetry 220,563 vs 220,566 lines. Compile 16.19-16.27G vs 16.17G and run 27.81G vs 27.76G are therefore noise on an identical program (about 0.2-0.6%; use this as the noise floor). Prediction 1 held, 3 held, 4 held (cycle on </2 remains with GUARDCMP=all), prediction 2 missed: no compile saving, because a guard of type tests already becomes the same type test as a typed head.
Meaning: a typed head and a guarded head are already one thing to the compiler. An extern head adds exactly one fact on top of a typed head: the clause has no body of its own, it is the extern.
Coordination facts received: Type System's #592 (fz-9x7.6) halves continuation allocations on the distiller (74.2M -> 38.1M), so the prompt rule's saving must be re-measured on top of #592 before a decision. Exceptions: a raise does not jump; the raising frame returns 0 and every frame above returns 0 to run_quantum, which resumes the handler from Process::delivered. A plain native frame in between is fine if it returns 0 on seeing its callee diverged (Process::diverged covers failed or a raise waiting); a function owning a try must not be called the new way.

Re-measured on #592 (fz-9x7.6, 3f7328f1e), same spike patch applied cleanly, release, 32,000 lines, stdout identical in all four, two runs each.
Distiller instructions: off 24.15G; narrow 22.15G (-8.3%); rule A 21.64G (-10.4%); rule B 20.83G (-13.8%). On the old base (#585) these were 28.81G / -13.4% / -16.3% / -22.8%. Absolute saving: narrow 3.87G -> 2.00G, A 4.68G -> 2.51G, B 6.57G -> 3.32G: about half, as Type System said.
Binary: 3,707,000 / 3,483,016 / 3,461,112 / 3,433,464 bytes. Peak RSS: 287 / 288 / 279 / 360 MB. User time 1.04 / 0.96-1.02 / 0.95-1.05 / 0.90-0.92 s.
Byte walk p1b: 96.2G / 66.8G / 66.8G / 64.1G; peak 674 MB except rule B 5,857 MB.

X5 instructions instead of C calls (user's direction: reduce +/2 on two integers to an instruction). Base #592 + narrow spike; switch FZ_SPIKE_INTRINSIC=1 emits fz_op_{add,sub,mul}_ii as an overflow-checked add/sub/mul and fz_op_{lt,lte,gt,gte,eq,neq}_ii as a compare. Predictions before the run: distiller 22.15G -> between 21.95G and 22.10G (under 1%: about 9.6M such calls at 10-15 instructions each); byte walk p1b 66.8G -> 61-64G; index walk larger in proportion; stdout identical; overflow still raises ArithmeticError with the same text.

X5 result (#592 + narrow, release, stdout identical, overflow output identical to the unchanged compiler).
Distiller: narrow 22.15G -> narrow+instructions 22.13-22.17G (no measurable change; predicted 0.2-0.9% lower: missed). Instructions without narrow: 24.10-24.13G vs 24.15G off (-0.1%).
Byte walk p1b: 66.8G -> 66.0G (-1.2%; predicted 61-64G: missed). Index walk p2b: 72.3G -> 70.1G (-3.0%).
Meaning: the C call itself costs about 5 instructions per operation. What is expensive is the continuation around the call (8.3% of the distiller, 31% of the byte walk on #592), not the call. Turning the extern into an instruction is worth about 0.1% on the distiller unless the split is removed too.

X1 and X2(a) results (builder, old base #585; I re-read the dumps and telemetry: executable counts 1375/1375/1329 and define_function 10,214/9,126/9,034 confirmed).
X1: unreferenced executables are not dropped today. With forwarder calls rewritten to the extern and unreachable forwarders dropped: 49 forwarders found, 282 call sites rewritten, 46 dropped (prediction 35-45: one over), 3 remain (compare, reached only as dispatch-edge arms). Run instructions equal narrow (24.96-24.98G vs 24.95G; prediction held). Binary 4,444,072 -> 4,440,952. Compile instructions of fz2 build: off 27.31-27.36G, narrow 24.50G (-10%), xhead 24.55G: the compile saving comes from narrow (fewer continuation functions: define_function 10,214 -> 9,126), not from dropping forwarders. Jobs naming a dropped specialisation: 260 of 12,855 (2.0%), 3.6% with function-keyed jobs, as an upper bound (prediction 2-4% held).
Found: 40 of 1,375 executables are unreachable in the unchanged program and are compiled anyway.
X2(a): 30 leaf loops, 10 execute. Full log: 38.6M entries, 11.1M iterations, longest run 12,892 (reverse_list), median run 0. skip_ws is entered 34.4M times and iterates 222,411 times: it is almost always a call that returns at once. digits: 3.58M entries, 9.1M iterations, longest 10. Prediction (max no more than longest line, median under 20) held.
X2(b) bail variant: not built (stopped after the user's direction to drop the wider rule). Rule B stays rejected on the memory result.
Direction from the user: replace calls with inlined fragments instead of the prompt rule. Page rewritten as version 3 on that basis.

User approved version 3 of the page ('proceed', 2026-11-14). This ticket is step 1: the splice. At a delivered direct call whose callee is an extern, or one clause with no dispatch and no steps that tail-calls an extern with the same parameters, the caller emits the extern as a step, branches to the existing raise on failure, and continues in the resume entry as a block. EffectSummary is removed. A reductions pin is added. Base: #592 (3f7328f1e). Acceptance: distiller 22.2G instructions or less on 32,000 lines (24.15G before); three paths match Elixir; falling pins lowered and listed; no pin rises without the user's authorization.

EffectSummary deletion moved to fz-sc8.218 with the user's approval (2026-11-14): about 190 test sites use the ExecutableEffects product as their vehicle. Builder finding: on #592 the splice does not change reductions_executed (200,000 before and after for 100,000 iterations); the fixture pins continuation_allocs 400,002 -> 100,001 and reductions as unchanged.
Landed as PR #600 (6783d2084), stacked on #592. Full gate green (6,521 passed), distiller 24.17G -> 22.16G, all pin changes are falls and are listed in the commit.

title: Arithmetic on known integers does not go through a continuation
